title: Before You Get Engaged… Read This Before You Promise Forever
paragraphs:
Before You Get Engaged… Read This Before You Promise Forever
The question isn't whether you've found someone you love. The question is whether both of you are walking toward the same Christ who can carry your covenant when feelings inevitably fail.
There is a kind of silence that settles into a room after a proposal.
Almost no one asks the question that could determine whether those two people will still be standing together fifty years from now.
"How much do you love each other?"
"Are you truly prepared to die to yourselves?"
But Scripture has always been more concerned with preparing hearts than planning ceremonies.
Many couples spend thousands preparing for one beautiful day.
God spends an entire Bible preparing us for one faithful lifetime.
Marriage was never created merely to make us happy.
Marriage was designed to make us holy.
That is why the very first marriage wasn't introduced with music, flowers, or celebration.

"Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh."
— Genesis 2:24
The Hebrew phrase is וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ (ve'davaq be'ishto).
It carries the idea of being glued together.
Bonded so deeply that separation tears both sides.
Marriage was never intended to be casual attachment.
The Hebrew word for covenant is בְּרִית (berit).
A covenant is stronger than a contract.
That changes everything before anyone ever says, "I do."
The Apostle Paul later reveals that marriage was never ultimately about us.
It was always pointing beyond us.

"This mystery is profound, and I am saying that it refers to Christ and the church."
— Ephesians 5:32
The Greek word translated "mystery" is μυστήριον (mystērion).
Something once hidden that God has now revealed.
Marriage is not merely about two sinners trying to coexist.
Marriage is a living sermon about Jesus Christ.
Every act of forgiveness reflects the Gospel.
Every act of patience reflects the Gospel.
When people look at Christian marriage, they should see Jesus before they notice personalities.
That is why engagement is so much more than preparing for a wedding.
It is preparing to become a visible testimony of Christ's redeeming love.
But this is where many believers unknowingly build their future on unstable ground.
Shared hobbies cannot replace shared surrender.
A beautiful wedding cannot compensate for an uncrucified heart.

"Seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness..."
— Matthew 6:33
Notice what He did not say.
Because whatever comes before Christ eventually becomes an idol.
Perhaps an even better question is,
"Am I becoming God's person for them?"
The Greek word translated repentance is μετάνοια (metanoia).
It literally describes a transformed mind that produces a transformed life.
Biblical repentance is not merely feeling guilty.
It is allowing God to completely redirect your heart.
Marriage desperately needs two people continually experiencing metanoia.
Not because they married the wrong person.
But because they remain imperfect people.
One of the greatest misunderstandings today is believing love alone sustains marriage.

"Love is patient and kind; love does not envy or boast; it is not arrogant or rude. It does not insist on its own way... Love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never ends."
— 1 Corinthians 13:4–8
The Greek word for love here is ἀγάπη (agapē).
Jesus demonstrated agapē before He ever commanded it.
"But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us."
Christ did not wait until we became lovable.
He loved us while we were rebels.
That is the standard marriage points toward.
Every Christian marriage is really two sinners continually receiving mercy from Christ and extending that same mercy to one another.
That is why forgiveness is not optional.

"I do not say to you seven times, but seventy-seven times."
— Matthew 18:22
It was mercy without keeping records.
Perhaps the greatest danger before engagement isn't marrying someone imperfect.
The danger is entering covenant while refusing discipleship.
Because marriage never fixes spiritual immaturity.
The Gospel never promises an easy marriage.
The Apostle Paul heard Jesus say,

"My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is made perfect in weakness."
— 2 Corinthians 12:9
The Greek word for grace is χάρις (charis).
Grace is not merely unearned favor.
That same grace sustains ordinary husbands.
Perhaps you're reading this while praying about someone.
Perhaps you've been married for years.
Or perhaps you're carrying deep scars from relationships that never became what you hoped.
Jesus is not only the Savior of souls.
He is also the Redeemer of broken stories.
The Gospel is filled with people whose lives were marked by scandal before they were transformed by grace.
None of them were defined forever by their failures.
Because Jesus rewrites stories that people thought were finished.
That is the heartbeat of the Gospel.
Not that perfect people find perfect spouses.
But that imperfect sinners find a perfect Savior.
Before you promise forever to another person...
Make sure you've first surrendered forever to Christ.
Because your spouse cannot carry the weight of being your savior.
Sit with it. Pray through it. Open the Scriptures again. Ask God not merely to prepare your future spouse, but to prepare you.

You never know who is quietly standing at the edge of a lifelong decision and needs biblical wisdom more than another opinion. Your testimony may become the encouragement someone else has been praying to read.
One faithful decision before the wedding may become the testimony that blesses generations long after the wedding photographs have faded.
